hypothesis: keccak256 runs through keccak-asm's NEON backend, whose EOR3/BCAX/RAX1/XAR paths are gated on target_feature = "sha3"; target-cpu=neoverse-v2 does not enable it, so Graviton4 emulates each with 2-3 instructions. Adding -C target-feature=+sha3 switches to the native SHA3 instructions. Keccak is ~19% of heavy-phase CPU, so expect a few % on c8g; test.sh's exact heavy-call hash checks correctness.
llm_commentary: Adding -C target-feature=+sha3 on Graviton4 (which target-cpu=neoverse-v2 does not imply) switches keccak-asm's NEON backend to the native SHA3 instructions; the on-box binary now has 1039 eor3/bcax/rax1/xar. c8g 6.72→6.56s (-2.4%, ranges 6.69-6.76 vs 6.53-6.60; THP back at madvise, so like-for-like with the parent), and test.sh's exact 10k-iteration keccak result passed. The gain is modest because keccak is ~19% of heavy-phase CPU and the emulated sequences were already only 2-3 instructions each. This flag belongs in the c8g family's build flags, alongside +sha2,+aes for crates that use them; exp-native should capture it plus the rest of the native feature set.
